newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares turn tail, end lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares turn tail, end lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Delhi shares reversed early gains to close sharply lower on Thursday as heavy profit-taking dominated the market, brokers said.

The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index closed 28.39 points, or 3.65 percent, lower at 748.63 points. After 30 minutes of trade, the index had gained four percent, piercing the 800-point barrier at 802.10.
"The fall in heavy-weighted stocks was a technical correction which was expected as market was in a overbought position," said a broker who asked not to be identified.
Traders said profit-taking by speculators dominated trading on almost all the counters.

"It seems the assurances given by the government for the capital market's revival have now been discounted as the buying interest has dropped substantially," said Shree Bhagwan Garg of brokers Means Leasing.
Last week, Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda reiterated his commitment to boost industry and economic reforms at an internaional business conference in Calcutta.
He said the government would announce measures to attract more private domestic and foreign investment before he left later this month for an annual world economic summit at Davos in Switzerland.
On December 31, Deve Gowda told industrialists in New Delhi that the government planned to announce moves to boost capital markets by mid-January.
Reliance Industries closed 15.10 rupees lower at 236.10, on speculative selling, brokers said.
ACC fell 113 rupees to 1,480 on speculative selling in the absence of any buying support.
State Bank of India lost 18.10 rupees to close at 271.50.
Larsen and Toubro eased 13 rupees to 249.
